summary: Designed and implemented a complete query language (PNQ) and Python API (PointerNetworkQuery) for the pointer network. The system supports graph traversal, search, pathfinding, impact analysis, edge suggestions, and shared-neighbor analysis across all 310 nodes and 4820 edges.

query_language_spec.name: PNQ (Pointer Network Query)
query_language_spec.description: A mini query language for agents to interrogate the pointer network. Supports both structured PNQ strings and direct Python API calls.

syntax_examples.query: FIND nodes WHERE domain = "scripts" AND weight >= 5
syntax_examples.description: Search for script nodes with high-weight edges
Find the highest-weight path between two nodes
Find all primary-strength neighbors within 2 hops
Show what's affected if SCR-0043 changes
Recommend missing edges using structural/tag/domain heuristics
Find common neighbors of two nodes
Which SOP pairs share the most common neighbors

where_clauses.tag = \"<value>\": Filter by shared tags in reasons

neighbors.description: BFS neighbor discovery with weight/strength filtering. Direction can be outgoing, incoming, or both.
neighbors.returns: List of {id, distance, weight, strength, path, domain}

find_path.description: Pathfinding with four strategies. 'weight' maximizes total edge weight via Dijkstra. 'hops' minimizes hop count via BFS. 'strength' prefers primary edges. 'hybrid' maximizes weight * strength_score.

search.signature: search(tags=None, domain=None, min_weight=0, strength=None, reasons_contain=None, limit=50)
search.description: Filtered search across all nodes. Supports domain, weight, strength, tag, and reason-text filters.
search.returns: List of {id, domain, edge_count, max_weight, edges}

impact.description: Reverse-dependency analysis. Traces all nodes that point TO the given node (directly or transitively). Identifies critical high-weight dependents.
impact.returns: {total_affected, direct_dependents, transitive_dependents, by_distance, by_strength, by_domain, critical_dependents}

suggest_edges.description: Recommends missing edges using three heuristics: (1) structural holes (reachable in 2 hops but not 1), (2) tag affinity via tag_clusters, (3) domain bridges to underrepresented domains.
suggest_edges.returns: List of {target, score, reason, via, domain}

shared_neighbors.description: Find nodes that both nodes point to, with weight details from each side.

most_shared_pairs.description: Find which pairs of nodes in a domain share the most outgoing neighbors.

execute.description: Parse and execute a PNQ query string. Dispatches to the appropriate method.

stats.description: Network summary: node/edge counts, domain/weight/strength/reason distributions.

design_decisions: Used BFS for neighbors() and hop-count pathfinding; Dijkstra (with negated weights) for weight/strength/hybrid pathfinding
Built reverse adjacency index at load time for efficient impact analysis and incoming-edge traversal
Query language uses a simple keyword-based grammar (FIND/PATH/NEIGHBORS/IMPACT/SUGGEST/SHARED/STATS) that is easy for agents to generate
suggest_edges() combines three complementary heuristics: structural holes (graph topology), tag affinity (semantic similarity via tag_clusters), and domain bridges (cross-domain coverage gaps)
All results include domain metadata so agents can filter by context
CLI supports both structured subcommands (neighbors, path, etc.) and free-form PNQ queries via the 'query' subcommand
integration_notes: Works with existing route_tracker.py — agents can use pointer_query to plan routes, then route_tracker to log them
The execute() method enables agents to pass natural-language-like queries without knowing the Python API
